London, 8<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Cash-strapped auto suppliers** will be able to tap only $3.5 billion in federal aid, not the $5 billion previously thought, because Ford won’t take its allocation of the funds.  In addition, GM will have to pay $100 million into the supplier bailout program so its suppliers can access its share of the federal funds, amounting to $2 billion.  GM is required to provide a 5 percent match to the $2 billion that the U.S. Treasury Department will make available to GM suppliers.  This week the feds are expected to present the final rules for a $5 billion supplier bailout program that was approved last month. But the terms mean that the $5 billion available to suppliers, already short of the $18.5 billion the supplier industry had sought, will be whittled down to $3.5 billion.  GM has asked for $2 billion of the amount for its suppliers, while Chrysler has asked for $1.5 billion for its suppliers.  The remaining $1.5 billion was earmarked for suppliers to Ford, but Ford said last month that it had enough cash for suppliers so that it did not need to participate. The association helped to broker the bailout program.  The programme would benefit suppliers in two ways: They can pay a 3% fee to get paid quicker than the normal 45 days for parts already delivered, or they can use the funds to guarantee their receivables as collateral for loans.  Either way, GM and Chrysler must select the suppliers that are eligible for the program. For that right, GM and Chrysler must provide a 5 percent match for the money being set aside for their suppliers, De Koker said. That amount would be $75 million for Chrysler’s $1.5 billion share of the programme. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**GM said its China sales** in March rose 24.6% from a year earlier to 137,004 vehicles, setting a company record for monthly sales as China’s stimulus policies bolstered the market.  GM, which faces the threat of bankruptcy if it cannot complete a reorganization by a U.S. government-imposed June 1 deadline, also attributed the strong sales growth in China, its second-largest market, to new product offerings. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Fiat ‘s equity stake in Chrysler** would be allowed to increase in blocks of 5% points as Fiat reaches certain benchmarks in bringing technology to its potential U.S. partner.  A person familiar with the FiatChrysler negotiations reiterated earlier reports that Fiat’s initial stake would be 20% if the companies complete an alliance.  Fiat then would be allowed to boost that share to 35% in stages as platform and powertrain technologies are transferred to the United States.  But the U.S. task force overseeing the bailouts of GM and Chrysler asked the Italian automaker to take a reduced stake from the outset. And before Fiat can increase its share to 35%, Chrysler has to pay back its U.S. government bailout money. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Moody’s** Investors Service said it still sees

a 70% chance of bankruptcy for Detroit’s automakers, given the difficulty of winning sweeping concessions from creditors out of court.  While the Obama administration would prefer that GM and Chrysler restructure outside of bankruptcy, it is clearly putting bankruptcy forward as an option, the ratings agency said.  Moody’s said Chrysler faces a more difficult burden in demonstrating its viability than does GM, and has the highest risk of filing for bankruptcy. It said Ford’s bankruptcy risk is moderately below 70%.  In the event of a bankruptcy filing by any of the Detroit 3, there is a high likelihood that the government will act to prevent a free-fall or uncontrolled bankruptcy in order to contain the severe disruption to the supply base and the broader economy. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Germany’s grand coalition cabinet** agreed to pledge more money for its car-scrapping scheme, a person close to the government said.  Angela Merkel’s government wants to pledge a further EUR5 billion to persuade 2 million car owners to scrap their vehicle, if it’s at least nine years old, and buy a new model.  The legislation will be valid through Dec. 31 and won’t be extended further. _Source:  Fx Street_
